rows.label: People present at an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest who could start CPR

source.title: Chocron et al. (2021), Bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation quality: potential for improvements in cardiac arrest resuscitation, Journal of the American Heart Association 10:e017930
source.quote: 35.2% had one bystander, 33.3% had 2 bystanders, and 31.5% had ≥3 bystanders

rows.explainer: In 9-1-1 recordings of arrests in King County, Washington (2017), arrests with bystander CPR had one bystander in 35%, two in 33% and three or more in 32%: about two on average. Not everyone present could start CPR (children, frail spouses), 71% of US arrests happen at home (CARES 2025 national summary, https://mycares.net/sitepages/uploads/2026/CARES%202025%20Non-Traumatic%20National%20Summary%20Report.pdf), where one or two family members are usually there, and arrests without bystander CPR more often have a lone witness. 1.5, from 1 to 3 (a public arrest).
